info.title: Flatline API
info.description: Monitoring API for automation and agents. Every response includes an `ok` boolean. Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Credential families: `flatline_op_...` operator (GUI sign-in and every /api/v1 call), `flatline_agent_push_...` host agent (only /api/push/{token} and /agent/*), `flatline_agent_backup_...` backup agent (only /api/backup/v1). Using a credential on the wrong surface returns an explicit error code with a `hint`. Failures use `{ ok, error, code, message, hint?, details? }`.

bearerAuth.description: Operator token `flatline_op_...` from the dashboard's Agents panel, or the admin token from data/initial-token.txt. Legacy `flatline_...` tokens are still accepted. Agent tokens are rejected here with `agent_token_on_operator_api`.

cookieAuth.name: fl_session
cookieAuth.description: The web app's session cookie, set by POST /api/v1/auth/session. It holds a random session id (`fls_...`), never a token; the server stores only its hash. A session belongs to a member account or an operator token and ends when it is signed out, after 30 idle days (account) or 400 (token), when the account is removed or its password reset or changed, or when the token is disabled, expires or is deleted. A cookie-authenticated request other than GET/HEAD/OPTIONS must send `X-Flatline-CSRF: 1`, or it is refused with 403 `csrf_required`.

monitorId.name: id
monitorId.description: Monitor id owned by the token's user.

error.description: Stable machine-readable error code. Same value as `code`.

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code. Same value as `error`.

message.description: What went wrong, in one sentence.

hint.description: What to do next. Names the fix or the required credential family; present on auth and validation failures.

details.description: Structured context for the error, e.g. the active run id or the conflicting field.

tokenKind.description: Kind of credential that was presented, when the error is about credential kind.

expectedTokenKind.description: Kind of credential the endpoint expects.

expectedPrefix.description: Prefix to mint the expected credential with.

retryAfterSeconds.description: Delay to wait before retrying a 429/503.

docs.description: Relative link to the LLM/runbook documentation.

metricCpuThreshold.description: Alert when server-derived CPU stays at or above this percent for 60s. null disables.

metricRamThreshold.description: Alert when RAM stays at or above this percent for 60s. null disables.

metricDiskThreshold.description: Alert when the fullest reported mount stays at or above this percent for 60s. null disables.

pushFailuresAck.description: Agent `failedPushes` value the operator last acknowledged; the board shows the difference.

samplesDroppedAck.description: Agent `samplesDropped` value the operator last acknowledged; the board shows the difference.

collectorErrorsAck.description: Acknowledged per-collector `agent.collectorErrors` counts, keyed by collector name.

mute.description: This monitor's own mute as a subject, or null. `monitors` lists the snapshot monitors still down; `hostMuted` is true when the monitor itself is among them (its own CPU/RAM and backup alerts are then silenced too); `smartFailed` and `fullMounts` are the disk problems present at mute time.

mutedBy.description: Subjects whose active mute covers this monitor; empty when not muted. A group is covered when it is down and every down monitor inside it is covered.

pushToken.description: Host-agent push token (`flatline_agent_push_...`). Bearer secret: keep it on the host.

notificationIDList.description: Map of notification id to enabled.

metricCpuThreshold.description: 1-100, or null to disable. See the Monitor schema for alert semantics.

reportedVersion.description: Backup-agent version last reported by this agent (run start or self-update check-in); null before the first report.

updateStatus.description: Outcome of the host's last self-update attempt: `ok` or a code such as `checksum_mismatch`, `downgrade_refused`, `lock_timeout`, `server_mismatch`. Null before the first check-in.

name.description: Lowercase ASCII letters, digits, hyphens and underscores; 1-64 characters, starting with a letter or digit.

monitorId.description: Optional server-monitor link. Removing the monitor unlinks without deleting the agent.

encrypted.description: Whether the bundle is age-encrypted. Absent means true (agents before optional encryption always encrypted).

agentVersion.description: Version of the sending agent (e.g. `0.3.0`). Recorded on the agent; not part of the idempotent same-run comparison, so a retried start may carry a newer version.

version.description: Running backup-agent version, `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` with an optional `-pre`/`+build` suffix.

updateStatus.description: Outcome of the last update attempt (`ok` or a snake_case code). Null keeps the stored value.

version.description: Backup-agent version this image ships (VERSION-BACKUP); null when the image ships none.

User.description: A member account. Every account has full permission, the same as an operator token. Passwords never appear in a response.

mustChangePassword.description: The password was set by someone else (add or reset); the member must choose their own at sign-in before anything else works.

startingPasswordExpired.description: A starting password unchanged for more than 7 days. Sign-in refuses it; someone must reset it.

tokenCount.description: Operator tokens this account minted (list and detail only).

Unauthorized.description: Missing, invalid, expired or inactive token.

Forbidden.description: `csrf_required` (a cookie write without `X-Flatline-CSRF: 1`) or `password_change_required` (an account still on its starting password).

get.summary: Load history charts and percentile statistics
get.description: Requires read scope. Extracts only CPU/RAM/first-GPU/first-VRAM scalars. Windows up to 7 days read raw archived snapshots (normally 30s) with nearest-rank percentiles; longer windows up to 17520 hours (2 years) read hourly rollups (min/max/average per metric), where percentiles describe hourly averages while peak stays the true maximum of the underlying readings. Returns at most 240 chart buckets, stats with count/min/max/mean/p90/p95/p99, coverage timestamps, and capped=true if the newest 50,000-row safety limit truncates the window. GPU/VRAM are null when unavailable. No data is represented as missing, not zero.

200.description: Window, coverage, percentile statistics, and bucket-average chart series

get.description: Requires read scope and Authorization header (never a URL token). SSE JSON data frames: ready, heartbeat {monitorId,patch}, metrics {monitorId,time,metrics}, invalidate, unauthorized. On ready/invalidate, resnapshot REST before applying buffered deltas. No replay log. Keepalive every 15s; credentials revalidated every 15s; reconnect after 15 minutes. Bounded to 8 streams/key, 128 total, and 256KiB pending output per stream.

parameters.name: metrics
parameters.description: 0 suppresses telemetry for ordinary monitor dashboards.

get.description: Machine-readable list of endpoints. Requires the `read` scope.
No token. 200 only when `SELECT 1` answers within 2 s and the check engine's watchdog ticked within 30 s; used by the container healthcheck.
Requires the `read` scope. Counts up/down/pending/maintenance/paused.

503.description: The database query failed; the summary is unknown, not zero.

get.description: Requires the `read` scope. Returns each valid `type`, plus `writableFields`, the allowlist accepted by POST and PATCH.
Requires the `read` scope. Scoped to the token's user. Supports `?status=`, `?tag=`, `?active=`, `?q=`, `?page=`, `?perPage=`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Substring match on name or url.

post.description: Requires the `write` scope. Unknown fields are ignored and returned in `ignoredFields`; `user_id` is never writable. Starts checking immediately unless `active` is false.

get.description: Requires the `read` scope. Beside the list's fields, carries `notificationIds`: the notifications this monitor alerts through (set with `notificationIDList` on create and update), ascending.

404.description: No such monitor for this user.

patch.description: Requires the `write` scope. Only supplied fields change. `type` cannot be changed after creation.

404.description: No such monitor for this user.

delete.description: Requires the `write` scope. For groups, `?deleteChildren=true` also deletes descendants; otherwise they are unlinked and kept.

get.description: Requires the `read` scope. `?limit` defaults to 100, max 1000.

post.description: Requires the `write` scope. Acknowledges the agent's current `agent.failedPushes` counter: the board shows `failedPushes - pushFailuresAck`. The ack is dropped automatically when the agent restarts and the counter moves backwards, so new failures are never masked.

Requires the `write` scope. Acknowledges every agent warning counter at once: `agent.failedPushes`, `agent.samplesDropped` and the per-collector `agent.collectorErrors`. The board shows each reported counter minus its ack, so this clears the whole "Agent: …" line on a card. Docker collector errors are acknowledged too, though the card renders them in the container section. The counters reset when the agent restarts and the acks are dropped automatically, so new warnings are never masked.

Snapshot what is down on the monitor (itself and the websites linked to it) and the disks its latest sample reports failing or full. The board shows the outage dark red and Telegram stops repeating it. Anything new on the monitor (another linked monitor down, a newly failing or newly full disk) deletes the mute, and so does full recovery. Muting again replaces the snapshot. 400 when nothing on the monitor is down.

400.description: Nothing on the monitor is down

delete.description: Delete the monitor's own mute and every mute covering it; for a group, every mute covering a monitor inside it. Idempotent: `unmuted` is empty when nothing was muted.

200.description: The subjects whose mute was deleted

get.description: Requires the `read` scope. `telegramBotToken` is redacted. Only the `telegram` type exists in this build.
Requires the `read` scope. 404 when the monitor has no samples yet.

404.description: No samples yet, or no such monitor.

get.description: Requires the `read` scope. Newest first. `hours` defaults to 24, max 168. At most 1000 rows; `capped` reports truncation.
Public. `setupNeeded` is true while no member account exists; the sign-in page then offers "Create the first account".

post.description: Public. Body `{token, email, name, password}`: any valid operator token (for example the first-boot token in `data/initial-token.txt`) creates the first member account, with the password as typed (no change required), and signs it in (sets the `fl_session` cookie). Without a valid operator token: 401 `unauthorized`, or 401 `agent_token_on_operator_api` for an agent token. Once any account exists: 409 `setup_done`; add further members with `POST /api/v1/users`.

200.description: Created and signed in; Set-Cookie carries the session. Body `{ok, principal:"account", user}`.

post.description: Unauthenticated, rate limited. Verifies password (+ TOTP when enrolled) and mints a full-scope token returned exactly once. Login tokens expire after 30 days.

401.description: Bad credentials, or TOTP required (error two_factor_required).

post.description: Public. Body `{email, password}` signs a member in and answers `{ok:true, principal:"account", mustChangePassword}`; body `{token}` signs in with an operator token and answers `{ok:true, principal:"token", tokenKind:"operator"}`. On success sets the `fl_session` cookie (`HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/; Max-Age=34560000`, plus `Secure` behind HTTPS) holding a new session id. A wrong email and a wrong password answer the same 401 `unauthorized`; a right password whose starting password expired (unchanged for 7 days) answers 401 `starting_password_expired`. Failed email/password attempts are limited to 5 per email and 20 per client address in 15 minutes, each counted before its password is checked; past that, even the right password answers 429 `rate_limited` with `retryAfterSeconds`. A bad token answers 401 `unauthorized`, an agent token 401 `agent_token_on_operator_api`, a busy token store 503; none of them set a cookie.

200.description: Signed in; Set-Cookie carries the session

401.description: Wrong email or password, or not an operator token

429.description: `rate_limited`: too many failed sign-ins for this email or address.

delete.description: Public. Ends the session server-side and clears the `fl_session` cookie; works with a missing or already-ended session.

200.description: Signed out; Set-Cookie clears the session

post.description: Public. A screen with no session asks to sign in. Returns the request `code` (shown as a QR code at `<base>/device#<code>`), a private `pollSecret` that only the screen keeps, `expiresIn` seconds and the instance `publicUrl`. 429 `busy` when too many screens are waiting.

Public. Body `{code, pollSecret}`. Returns status `pending`, `denied`, `expired` or `approved`; an approved response carries a new operator `token` that never expires. A wrong secret or unknown code reads as `expired`. The token is minted on the first poll after approval and can be fetched again for 60 seconds. A screen approved by a member who was removed before that first poll reads as `denied`.
Operator token. Body `{code}`. Returns the screen's user agent, how long it has waited and a suggested name. 404 when the request is unknown, expired or already answered.

Operator token. Body `{code, name}` (name 1 to 60 characters). The screen then receives its own operator token, listed in `/api/v1/api-keys` under that name. 409 `not_pending` when already answered or expired.
Operator token. Body `{code}`. 409 `not_pending` when already answered or expired.

get.description: Says who the credential acts as: `principal:"account"` with `account:{id, email, name, mustChangePassword}` for a member's session, or `principal:"token"` with `token:{id, name}` for a bearer token or token session. Also states the credential family and capabilities. An agent token answers 401 `agent_token_on_operator_api` with the expected prefix.

200.description: The principal, credential kind (`operator`), capabilities and agent-endpoint map.

get.description: Requires the `read` scope. One query for up to 200 monitors; unknown ids and monitors without samples come back as null entries. Register before /monitors/{id}/metrics/latest so Express does not read "metrics" as an id.

200.description: Samples keyed by monitor id, null where missing

get.summary: List operator tokens (metadata only). Each key reports `maker`: `{id, name, removed}` for a key minted by a member (on the Tokens page or by approving a QR sign-in), or `null` for one minted with a bearer token or token session, and every key from before accounts. `removed: true` (and `id: null`) once that member's account is gone.

post.summary: Mint an API key. The plaintext token is returned exactly once. A member's session records them as the key's `maker`.

patch.summary: Enable or disable an API key (`active` required).

503.description: Storage failure; transient. Carries `Retry-After` (seconds, 5-30, jittered). Retry the same sample.

post.summary: Push with an optional `metrics` body. Invalid metrics, or a non-empty body that is not JSON, answer 400 while the heartbeat stays recorded; storage failures answer 503 with `Retry-After`.

400.description: Validation failure (permanent): invalid metrics or a body that is not JSON. The heartbeat, if any, was recorded.

404.description: Unknown or paused monitor, or out-of-range ping.

503.description: Storage failure; transient. Carries `Retry-After` (seconds, 5-30, jittered). Retry the same sample.

get.summary: Average ping badge (SVG); duration like `24h`, default 24h.
Average response badge (SVG); hours, default 24, max 720.
Resolve a hostname to a status page slug (public).
Status page config, pinned incidents and public groups (password gated).
Public heartbeat lists and 24h uptime per monitor (password gated).

post.summary: Unlock a password-protected status page; sets the `fl_status_auth` cookie.

get.description: Requires the `read` scope. One query for up to 200 servers; each entry holds the raw stored links and their resolved monitors with current status. Servers without links are absent. Register before /monitors/{id} so the static path wins.

Requires the `read` scope. One strip per monitor: `buckets` buckets, oldest first, the last one containing now. Buckets are aligned to multiples of `bucketSeconds` since the Unix epoch (bucket index = floor(epochSeconds / bucketSeconds)), so a client can place a live beat itself; `start` is the UTC start of the first bucket. A bucket is `[worstStatus, beats, failedBeats]` (status 0 down, 1 up, 2 pending, 3 maintenance; worst by severity down > pending > maintenance > up) or `null` when it has no heartbeats. Unknown ids are absent from `strips`; groups are included. Omitting `ids` returns the first 200 monitors by id. `hours * 3600 / buckets` must be a whole number of seconds, at least 60. Cached for about 10 seconds. Register before /monitors/{id} so the static path wins.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated monitor ids, at most 200. Omit for all monitors (first 200).

get.description: Requires the `read` scope. `raw` is the stored links (each may be a group); `resolved` expands groups to their non-group descendants, deduplicated, each with current status and the link it came through (`via`).

put.description: Requires the `write` scope. Body `{ linkedMonitorIds: number[] }` (up to 200) becomes the server's links exactly; unknown ids are skipped, self-links and duplicates dropped.

delete.description: Requires the `write` scope. Removes every link for the server.

get.description: Lists linked and unlinked agents newest-first. Omit `monitorId` for every agent; limit 1-200, cursor is an agent UUID.

post.description: Returns the dedicated credential in plaintext exactly once. Only its hash is stored.

patch.description: Accepts name, monitorId (null unlinks), enabled, intervalSeconds and retentionCount.

post.description: Returns a replacement credential once and invalidates the previous one.
The agent and its run history remain; the credential stops authenticating immediately.

get.description: Newest-first paginated run history. Cursor is a run UUID.

post.description: Operator only. Archive verification and actual restore verification are separate states; agents cannot self-assert a restore.

post.summary: Start or replay an upload run
post.description: Agent credential only. `(agentId, clientRunId)` is unique; identical retries return the existing run, conflicting parameters answer 409. One uploading or finalizing run per agent.

409.description: Machine-readable `error`: `active_run` (another run of this agent is uploading or finalizing; the body adds `activeRunId` and `activeClientRunId` so the agent can resume it with the same clientRunId or abandon it), `params_conflict` (clientRunId exists with different parameters) or `run_terminal` (failed, pruned, deleting or otherwise not reopenable). Only `params_conflict` and `run_terminal` mean the local bundle can never be delivered.

get.description: Agent credential only. Access to another agent run answers 404.

404.description: Run not found for this agent.

put.description: Agent credential only. The body is the next sequential byte range; index is offset / 8388608, non-final chunks are exactly 8 MiB. Authenticate before reading the body. Successful replies include the committed offset. Byte-identical retries are idempotent; conflicting bytes or offsets answer 409.

400.description: Invalid index or non-final chunk size.

404.description: Run not found for this agent.

507.description: Office storage reserve would be violated.

post.description: Idempotent. Full digest and size are verified before the bundle is fsynced and atomically published; a mismatch answers 422 and never becomes completed.

404.description: Run not found for this agent.

409.description: `conflict` when bytes are missing, `run_terminal` when the run is failed, expired or pruned.

503.description: `busy`: another request holds this run. Retry after `Retry-After` seconds.

422.description: Full digest mismatch; the run is failed.

post.description: Agent credential only. Used when the agent no longer holds the bundle of its active run (for example after quarantining it), so a new export can be delivered. The run becomes `failed` with `upload_abandoned`, its capacity reservation is released and maintenance removes its bytes. Idempotent.

404.description: Run not found for this agent.

409.description: `conflict` while finalizing, `run_terminal` when already completed or ended.

503.description: `busy`: a chunk or completion for this run is in flight.

post.description: Agent credential only. Accepts a bounded safe code even when no bytes were produced; clientRunId is 1-128 characters. Same clientRunId and code is idempotent. An uploading run can be failed; no other state is rewritten.

409.description: `run_terminal` when the run is finalizing, completed, deleting, pruned or expired (only an uploading run can be failed); `conflict` when the clientRunId was already reported with another code.

post.description: Operator only. Returns `{ok, runId, url, expiresAt}`. The URL is bound to this completed run, expires after about two minutes and is consumed by the first GET, so a browser can stream the bundle to disk with a plain navigation; no long-lived credential enters a URL.

404.description: Run is not a retained completed run.

get.summary: Download a bundle with a ticket
get.description: No Authorization header: the ticket from `download-ticket` is the credential. Streams the bundle like the operator download route, with `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`. Unknown, used and expired tickets answer 404.

200.description: Bundle: age-encrypted (`.age`) or plain tar (`.tar`), per the run's `sourceSummary.encrypted`

404.description: Ticket is unknown, used or expired.

get.description: Operator only. Streams the retained bundle as an attachment with `Cache-Control: no-store`. The URL carries no credential; use the operator Authorization header. Incomplete, failed, expired and pruned runs are not downloadable.

200.description: Bundle: age-encrypted (`.age`) or plain tar (`.tar`), per the run's `sourceSummary.encrypted`

post.description: Agent credential only. Records the version the agent runs and, when given, the outcome of its host's last self-update attempt, then answers with the backup-agent release this image ships. Run by `flatline-backup self-update` once per instance on the host, whether or not its backups are scheduled.

401.description: Invalid backup credential (operator and push tokens are refused).

get.description: Agent credential only. Streams `flatline-backup-<os>-<arch>` from the image's backup-agent directory with `Cache-Control: no-store`. Any other name (VERSION-BACKUP, checksums, telemetry builds) is a 404. Verify the bytes against the check-in's `sha256`.

404.description: No backup-agent build by that name.

post.summary: Add a member with a starting password (at least 10 characters). They must choose their own password at first sign-in; the starting password expires after 7 days. 409 `email_taken`, 400 `weak_password`.

get.summary: One member and the operator tokens they minted.

patch.summary: Change a member's name and/or email. 409 `email_taken`.

delete.description: Optional body `{revokeTokenIds: [id, ...]}`: operator tokens this member made (from `GET /api/v1/users/{id}`) to disable in the same step; any other id answers 400 and nothing changes. Tokens not listed keep working and keep the maker's name (`maker.removed: true`). The member's sessions end at once. Removing your own account answers 409 `cannot_remove_self`. Removing the last account is allowed: token sign-in always remains.

post.summary: Give a member a new starting password (at least 10 characters). They must change it at their next sign-in; every session they have ends now.

post.description: For a member's session only (a bearer token or token session answers 400 `not_an_account`). Body `{currentPassword, newPassword}`; a wrong current password answers 400 `wrong_password`, a new one under 10 characters 400 `weak_password`, a new one equal to the current one 400 `same_password`, and an expired starting password 401 `starting_password_expired`. Success clears `mustChangePassword` and ends the account's other sessions; this one stays signed in. An account with a starting password can reach only this route, `GET /api/v1/auth/me` and sign-out; everything else answers 403 `password_change_required`.
